positioning: The first seven days of Christmas. Twenty-eight dogs so far.
story: Every carol has a list. This one has dogs.

The old song counts twelve days of gifts. Ours counts twelve days of dogs, starting today, Sunday, December 20. A Poodle sits in the pear tree. Every day after that, a bigger group joins her in the same snowy courtyard.
Two Dachshunds dig. Three Huskies haul. Four Corgis crawl. Five Golden Pups tumble. Six Greyhounds race. Seven Beagles bounce. By Saturday the courtyard holds 28 dogs.
The tune is old. It first appeared in print in England in 1780, in a children’s book. The pear tree stayed. The partridge, we decided, was a Poodle.
Keep the cookies up high and the tinsel off the floor. A dog’s idea of a present is anything that smells like dinner.
Turn the page. The Poodle is waiting.
rank_cap: dogs in the courtyard by Saturday
fblocks: The Twelve Days of Christmas appeared in England in 1780. It was a children’s rhyme, not a hymn.
Poodle, from the German Pudel, to splash. Dachshund, the badger dog. Greyhound, the fastest of the lot.
Chocolate, raisins and xylitol are dangerous for dogs. Tinsel and ribbon can block the gut. Keep all of it out of reach.
Keep it loose and keep bows off the neck. A dog must be able to shake, sit and breathe.
28 dogs by Saturday. 78 by New Year’s Eve. 12 days. 1 pear tree.
days: One Poodle, one pear tree, and no plan for getting down.
Dachshund means badger dog in German. Two of them will dig to the gifts.
Sled dogs raced serum to Nome in 1925. Three Huskies haul gifts instead.
Welsh legend says fairies rode Corgis. Four now crawl toward the cookies.
Five Golden Pups pile into the sled. Wisdom is knowing when to just ride.
Greyhounds top 40 miles an hour. On Christmas Day, six of them choose a circle.
Seven Beagles bounce at the gate and sing for the sake of it. The yard sings back.
last_walk:
The snow keeps falling on the courtyard.
Twenty-eight dogs are settling in for the night. The Poodle still holds her branch. The Greyhounds slept where they stopped. Stay a minute by the lights. Eight Bernese are on their way.
